title: NY S08831: Provides for the use of automated employment decision-making tools and artificial intelligence systems by a county, city, town, village, school district, board of cooperative educational services, county vocational education and extension board, district corporation, the state university of New York, the city university of New York, or community college; amends the effectiveness thereof.

obligations: Any covered entity that utilizes an automated employment decision-making tool shall, to the extent feasible, publish a list of such tools on its website no later than the thirtieth of December next succeeding the date this section becomes law, and annually thereafter (Sec. 6, state technology law section 402-a).

To the extent feasible, the disclosure shall include a description of the tool, the date use began, a summary of the purpose and use, and any other information deemed relevant by the covered entity (Sec. 6, state technology law section 402-a).
prohibitions: The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not affect the existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement or the existing representational relationships among employee organizations or the bargaining relationships between the employer and an employee organization (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).

The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not result in the discharge, displacement or loss of position, including partial displacement such as a reduction in the hours of non overtime work, wages, or employment benefits, or result in the impairment of existing collective bargaining agreements (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).

The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not result in the transfer of existing duties and functions currently performed by employees to an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).

The use of an artificial intelligence system shall not alter the rights or benefits, and privileges, including but not limited to terms and conditions of employment and civil service status, and the collective bargaining unit membership status of all existing employees shall be preserved and protected (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).

Passed 2026-02-13. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This act repeals prior automated decision making provisions and adds a definition of covered entity. It requires covered entities that use automated employment decision making tools to publish a list of those tools on their websites annually. It also prohibits covered entities and specified public employers from using artificial intelligence systems to affect collective bargaining rights, displace employees, reduce hours wages or benefits, transfer duties, or alter employment terms and civil service status.

Who it applies to

  • county
  • city
  • town
  • village
  • school district
  • board of cooperative educational services
  • county vocational education and extension board
  • district corporation
  • state university of New York
  • city university of New York
  • community college
  • state or any agency or public authority thereof
  • public improvement district
  • special district

Effective date

The act takes effect immediately; sections 1 through 16 take effect on the same date and in the same manner as the 2025 chapter takes effect (Sec. 18). The 2025 chapter expires and is deemed repealed July 1, 2028 (Sec. 17).

Key definitions

  • covered entity: any county, city, town, village, school district, board of cooperative educational services, county vocational education and extension board, district corporation, the state university of New York, the city university of New York, or community college (Sec. 4, state technology law section 401 subdivision 3).

Obligations

  • Any covered entity that utilizes an automated employment decision-making tool shall, to the extent feasible, publish a list of such tools on its website no later than the thirtieth of December next succeeding the date this section becomes law, and annually thereafter (Sec. 6, state technology law section 402-a).
  • To the extent feasible, the disclosure shall include a description of the tool, the date use began, a summary of the purpose and use, and any other information deemed relevant by the covered entity (Sec. 6, state technology law section 402-a).

Prohibitions

  • The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not affect the existing rights of employees pursuant to an existing collective bargaining agreement or the existing representational relationships among employee organizations or the bargaining relationships between the employer and an employee organization (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).
  • The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not result in the discharge, displacement or loss of position, including partial displacement such as a reduction in the hours of non overtime work, wages, or employment benefits, or result in the impairment of existing collective bargaining agreements (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).
  • The use of artificial intelligence systems shall not result in the transfer of existing duties and functions currently performed by employees to an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).
  • The use of an artificial intelligence system shall not alter the rights or benefits, and privileges, including but not limited to terms and conditions of employment and civil service status, and the collective bargaining unit membership status of all existing employees shall be preserved and protected (Sec. 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).

Penalties and enforcement

The text does not state any enforcement authority, penalties, or private right of action.

How it affects AI deployment

  • Covered entities that use automated employment decision making tools must publish a list of those tools on their website by December 30 of the year after the section becomes law, and annually thereafter, including description, start date, purpose, and other relevant information (Sec. 6).
  • Covered entities and specified public employers cannot use artificial intelligence systems to affect collective bargaining rights, displace employees, reduce hours wages or benefits, transfer duties, or alter employment terms and civil service status (Sec. 7 through 15).
  • The act expires and is deemed repealed July 1, 2028, so these requirements are temporary (Sec. 17).

Notable exemptions

  • The disclosure obligation applies only to the extent feasible (Sec. 6).
  • No explicit exemptions from the prohibitions on artificial intelligence system use are stated in the text.

Compliance steps

  • Determine if the organisation is a covered entity as defined in Sec. 4 (county, city, town, village, school district, board of cooperative educational services, county vocational education and extension board, district corporation, state university of New York, city university of New York, or community college).
  • If using an automated employment decision making tool, publish a list of such tools on the organisation's website by December 30 of the year after the section becomes law, and annually thereafter, including description, date use began, summary of purpose and use, and any other relevant information (Sec. 6).
  • Ensure that use of artificial intelligence systems does not affect existing collective bargaining rights or representational or bargaining relationships (Sec. 7 through 15).
  • Ensure that use of artificial intelligence systems does not result in discharge, displacement, loss of position, reduction in hours of non overtime work, wages, or employment benefits, or impairment of collective bargaining agreements (Sec. 7 through 15).
  • Ensure that use of artificial intelligence systems does not transfer existing duties and functions currently performed by employees to an artificial intelligence system (Sec. 7 through 15).
  • Ensure that use of artificial intelligence systems does not alter rights, benefits, privileges, terms and conditions of employment, civil service status, or collective bargaining unit membership status (Sec. 7 through 15).
  • Monitor the expiration date of July 1, 2028, when the act is deemed repealed (Sec. 17).
